sample.title: Who dominates hybrid car sales?
sample.description:
Just three automakers control the majority of one of the hottest segments in the U.S. car market — and none of them are American companies.

In the first half of 2026, sales of hybrid cars — not long ago considered a bridge to fully electric vehicles — have risen nearly 20% year-over-year to a record market share of 15.4%, according to the Center for Automotive Research, almost three times the share of pure EVs.

CNBC's Robert Ferris has the details.

Find the full report in related video.

sample.title: How SpaceX's AI ambitions took over Memphis
sample.description:
Two years after Elon Musk made Greater Memphis the center of his artificial intelligence ambitions, building data centers and energy infrastructure at breakneck speed, residents are grappling with unwanted effects, including noise and emissions from the natural gas-burning turbines. 

Now, public opposition to the SpaceXAI sites, known as Colossus and Colossus II, is providing a blueprint for other communities across the country opposed to AI developments.

sample.title: How High Diesel Prices Are Creating A Hidden Tax For Consumers
sample.description:
California is home to the busiest containership ports in the country. Many of the goods that enter through those ports must travel hundreds or even thousands of miles before they reach distribution centers, meaning a portion of the supply chain pays California diesel prices-the most expensive in the U.S. CNBC’s Pippa Stevens breaks down what that means for consumers.

sample.title: Why Condos Are Getting Harder To Buy
sample.description:
Buying a condo may be about to become significantly more difficult, even for buyers with good financial standing. Beginning August 3rd, Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are making big changes to how condominium mortgages are reviewed. Streamlined review process that applied to many transactions will now be retired. Instead, lenders will now have to conduct a more comprehensive review of a the building before the mortgage can go to Fannie Mae or Freddie Mac.

Trump again targets US birthright citizenship | BBC News
sample.description:
President Donald Trump is trying again to scale back birthright citizenship in the US, weeks after the Supreme Court shot down his previous attempt to eliminate the right.
 
The president signed two executive orders on Thursday, including one that expands the existing definitions of non-citizens whose children are not eligible for birthright citizenship.
 
The second order bans so-called birth tourism, the practice of pregnant mothers coming to the US to give birth so that their babies will be citizens.
 
Trump and members of his administration have repeatedly railed against birth tourism, including accusing Russian and Chinese adversaries of taking advantage of birthright citizenship to infiltrate the US.

sample.title: Battle in the Black Sea - Russia and Ukraine intensify attacks on shipping | BBC News
sample.description:
Russia has been ramping up its efforts to strangle Ukraine's commercial links to the outside world, by launching waves of attacks along the country's Black Sea coastline.

While there have been Russian attacks on international vessels before, they've never been so numerous or so deadly. Ukraine's port administration says there were 57 Russian attacks on civilian vessels last month. Ukraine's once bustling ports – such as Odesa, Chornomorsk, and Pivdennyi – are almost devoid of ships.

Ukraine is also targeting shipping in the war, with recent, highly successful attacks on Russian vessels, including sanctioned tankers carrying oil, as well as ships involved in carrying supplies to Russian-occupied Crimea. 

Using its own drones, Ukraine has struck around 200 Russian vessels, bringing traffic in the strategic Sea of Azov to a virtual standstill.

sample.title: Iran says deal with Oman on Strait of Hormuz is in final stages | BBC News
sample.description:
Iran says it has reached an agreement with Oman on a route for shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei did not give any further details on the agreement, which he said was "in the final stages".

Baqaei warned, however, that a deal with Oman would not guarantee safe navigation through the strait, arguing security remained impacted by the US blockade of Iran's ports. 

Since the US and Israel attacked Iran in February, Tehran has largely blocked the Strait of Hormuz through which about a fifth of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas usually passes.
